identity.title: High-accuracy and dimension-free sampling with diffusions

problem.claim: Develop a diffusion-model solver that produces high-quality samples with high accuracy using approximate access to data-distribution scores.

gap.claim: Prior discretization methods reportedly have iteration complexity polynomial in ambient dimension and inverse accuracy, while a high-accuracy guarantee for a diffusion-based sampler using approximate scores was absent.

contributions.claim: A solver combining low-degree approximation with the collocation method.
A complexity bound that is polylogarithmic in inverse accuracy and depends on dimension only through the target distribution's effective support radius.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that this is the first high-accuracy guarantee for a diffusion-based sampler using approximate score access.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report proving polylogarithmic dependence on 1/ε for the proposed solver's iteration complexity.
The authors report that ambient dimension does not enter explicitly; its effect occurs through the effective radius of the target support.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diffusion models have achieved empirical success for sampling from multimodal distributions.
Inference requires numerically solving a differential equation without a closed form, and discretization typically needs many small iterations for high-quality samples.
Existing discretization analyses reportedly scale polynomially with ambient dimension and inverse accuracy.
The paper introduces a low-degree-approximation and collocation-based solver with polylogarithmic inverse-accuracy complexity and effective-radius dependence on dimension.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a concrete computational bottleneck to two separately stated complexity targets: inverse-accuracy dependence and dimension dependence.

lessons.interpretation: This decomposition makes the claimed advance easier to evaluate because each improvement has a distinct complexity axis.
lessons.application: When presenting a theoretical method, state baseline scaling and separate the target improvements by parameter, then attach each guarantee to its precise condition.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the main contribution is empirical or when complexity parameters cannot be meaningfully isolated.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact polylogarithmic expression, score-approximation assumptions, sampling-distance guarantee, or dependence on the effective radius.
No empirical comparisons, implementation details, or proof details are provided in the supplied units.
